title: git-vouch-trqp: TRQP bridge so OpenVTC verify-trust can check git-vouch signers
description: A separate, optional service (NOT part of the git-vouch single file, which stays a CLI with no service) that answers ToIP TRQP authorization queries from a git-vouch registry, so OpenVTC's verify-trust and other TRQP consumers can ask 'may this DID sign for the kernel?'. Facts from source (2026-10-22): verify-trust resolves a registry DID and picks TSP>DIDComm>HTTPS from its DID document, so HTTPS alone suffices; HTTPS answers are unsigned, trust rests on the DID-document-bound endpoint (~/GIT/OpenVTC_verifiable-git-infrastructure/crates/verify-trust/src/registry.rs:185-260). Query = {entity_id: signer DID, authority_id, action, resource(forge-qualified)} (src/lib.rs:1-45, src/resource.rs). Signer DID comes from the commit committer header; DID doc must publish the Ed25519 key in the sshsig. TRQP spec: ~/PROJECT/ToIP/spec/toip-trqp.md. Design constraint: the service is a thin stateless shim over 'git vouch query'; git-vouch stays the single source of truth for tier logic.
notes: UNPARKED (Mark 2026-10-22): build the bridge now (ultracode workstream B), overriding 'stays parked until OpenVTC moves'. Key types are now FIVE: RSA 2048-16384 accepted since aa80d0a (ssh-rsa, did:key rsa-pub 0x1205); verify-trust refuses ssh-rsa as it refuses all but plain ssh-ed25519 (docs/trqp-interop.md section 5). OpenVTC issue #169 still open; do not contact OpenVTC.
